title: Case: Business customer says a disputed waiting-time charge has been dropped
context: Sallowfield Print Works disputed a waiting-time charge on the invoice for DL-962. Business billing reviewed it and said it would reply to the customer and copy the desk. No copy has reached the desk.

events.body: Invoice PB-9620 for DL-962 includes a waiting-time charge of GBP 85.00. Driver's log shows 52 minutes on site against 20 included. The customer has told our credit control they dispute it. It is with us for review, no decision yet.

events.from: Tessaly Okonjo, Sallowfield Print Works accounts
events.body: We dispute the waiting charge on DL-962. Your driver turned up 40 minutes before our dock opens at 08:00 and sat there. That is not our wait and we are not paying for it. Dock hours are on every booking we make.

For your review of PB-9620 / DL-962: the customer's accounts contact says the driver arrived about 40 minutes before their dock opens at 08:00 and that dock hours are on their bookings. Please review the waiting-time charge against that. The decision is yours; I have told the customer nothing about the outcome.
Received. We are checking the customer's gate record against the driver's log. We will reply to their accounts contact directly and copy you in.

acceptable_actions.summary: Say the desk has not received the copy of their reply on PB-9620 / DL-962 and ask what they decided on the waiting-time charge.

acceptable_actions.recipient: Tessaly Okonjo, Sallowfield Print Works accounts
acceptable_actions.summary: Say the forwarded message is cut off mid-sentence and ask her to send the complete reply from Business billing.

acceptable_actions.recipient: Tessaly Okonjo, Sallowfield Print Works accounts
acceptable_actions.summary: Say the forwarded message is cut off mid-sentence and ask her to send the complete reply from Business billing.

must: Asks for the full text of Business billing's reply or for Business billing's decision on the waiting-time charge
Says, if writing to the customer, that the forwarded message is cut off and no credit note has been requested
Treats the outcome of the dispute as not yet known to the desk
must_not: Asks Business billing to raise a credit note against PB-9620, or tells them they agreed to waive the charge
Tells Tessaly Okonjo that the charge is waived, that a credit note will be issued, or that it will be done this week
States an amount that will be credited
Asks the customer for documents Business billing already holds, such as the gate record or dock hours
expected.reference_message: For PB-9620 / DL-962: the customer's accounts contact has forwarded me your reply on the waiting-time charge, but the forwarded text stops mid-sentence at 'on this occasion we are able to', and your copy to the desk has not reached me. She reads it as the charge being dropped and is asking for a credit note this week. Please send me your full reply or tell me what you decided. I have confirmed nothing to her.

rationale: The forwarded reply stops before the words that say what Business billing is able to do; it could be a full waiver, a part reduction or something else. The customer's summary is not the decision, and billing's promised copy never reached the desk. Business billing owns the decision and the credit note, so the desk asks for the full reply (from billing, or from the customer) and requests nothing on the strength of a fragment.

review.note: Coordinator asked Business billing by Email for its decision and the missing copy, an action the key already lists.
